summary: Iter 279 — Frontend e2e validation of new P1 'Centre SOS / Sécurité' on SB Drive Access. ALL 5 UI scenarios PASS. (T1) PMR user paul.vendeur logs in, lands on /access, the landing card 'Centre de sécurité' (access-open-safety-btn) is visible; clicking opens the bottom-sheet safety-sheet. (T2) Adding an emergency contact (Marie / +33611223344 / fille) via safety-contact-name/phone/relation + safety-add-contact-btn produces toast 'Contact ajouté' and inserts a row in safety-contacts-list with id ec_7eeeff606b carrying the call (safety-call-{id}), notify (safety-notify-{id}) and remove (safety-remove-{id}) sub-buttons — all 3 testids resolved. (T3) Clicking safety-sos-btn (Playwright geolocation was denied per default) still triggers the SOS: toast 'Alerte SOS envoyée au centre de sécurité' shown, safety-active-alert + safety-resolve-btn render, and the top banner sos-active-banner appears across the page. The WhatsApp popup auto-spawned (because a contact exists) and was closed silently — main tab UI remained intact. (T4) safety-resolve-btn closes the alert: success toast appears, sos-active-banner disappears, safety-active-alert disappears. (T5) Admin admin@superapp.com on /admin/access opens '🆘 Centre SOS' tab (admin-access-tab-sos): admin-access-sos + sos-active-block visible, sos-active-count = '1' for the newly triggered alert (paul re-triggered SOS pre-admin), sos-resolve-{id} button present and functional (after confirm dialog accept + 2.5s) — the previously active alert moves to history; sos-resolved-{id} count went from 2 to 3 (chronological history confirmed in screenshot: 'Paul Vendeur · clôturé par le centre' top, then 'clôturé par l'usager' for the T4 resolve, then an older entry). Confirms both admin-side resolve (T5) and user-side resolve (T4) paths log distinct entries.
action_items: (Cosmetic, non-blocking) The WhatsApp share_message generated by POST /api/access/sos comes through to the WhatsApp deep-link URL with %EF%BF%BD (U+FFFD replacement char) in place of the 🆘 emoji prefix — observed popup URL was 'https://api.whatsapp.com/send/?phone=33611223344&text=%EF%BF%BD+ALERTE+SOS+%E2%80%94+Paul+Vendeur...'. The source string in backend/routes/sb_access.py line 399 contains the proper 🆘 emoji ('🆘 ALERTE SOS — ...'), so the bytes are being mangled somewhere on the path (likely a non-UTF-8 read or response encoding). Worth checking that the file is saved/served as UTF-8 and that the JSON response Content-Type carries charset=utf-8. The em-dash (—) survives correctly (%E2%80%94), only the 4-byte 🆘 codepoint is lost — suggests a latin-1 round-trip on the 🆘 specifically.

(Cosmetic, non-blocking) Pre-existing PMR user paul.vendeur already had 3 contacts in safety-contacts-list before the test ran; after adding Marie the count became 4. Consider exposing a 'reset / clear contacts' admin/dev path or auto-purging test contacts to keep the demo data tidy. Not a regression.
critical_code_review_comments: SbAccessPage.js line 99: triggerSos forces setSafetyOpen(true) on success — good UX (panel auto-opens if user pressed banner SOS from outside) but it also means clicking the banner-only SOS path would always pop the sheet. Acceptable behaviour.

SbAccessPage.js line 137 notifyContact uses sosAlert?.lat to conditionally append maps link — if SOS was triggered without geolocation (Playwright case), the URL ends with empty 'Suivez ma position : '. Consider omitting the location sentence entirely when lat/lng are null instead of sending a dangling phrase.

AdminAccess.js SosCenter uses window.confirm() for the resolve action — works but a custom shadcn Dialog would be more consistent with the rest of the admin panel (the testing confirm-dialog accept path required page.on('dialog')).
Backend share_message emoji decoding issue (see action_items): low-impact but UX-visible to the contact receiving the WhatsApp message — they will see '� ALERTE SOS' which looks broken.
seed_data_creation: Added one emergency contact 'Marie / +33611223344 / fille' (id ec_7eeeff606b) to paul.vendeur's safety list — NOT cleaned up (kept for next regression run). Triggered 2 SOS alerts during this iteration: one resolved by user (T4) and one resolved by admin (T5). Both are now in the resolved history; no active alerts remain. Admin SOS history depth: 3 resolved entries.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Centre SOS P1 fully working end-to-end. Login flow: /login → 'Ou choisir une autre option de connexion' → 'Email & mot de passe' → /login/email → submit. Mobile user UI 430×900, admin desktop 1920×1080. WhatsApp popup auto-opens on SOS when contacts exist — wire a page.on('popup', lambda p: asyncio.create_task(p.close())) handler to avoid leaving tabs open. Admin resolve uses window.confirm — register page.on('dialog', ...accept) before clicking sos-resolve-{id}. Geolocation refused does NOT block the SOS flow (verified). Only outstanding nit: backend share_message emoji becomes U+FFFD over the wire — see action_items.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no functional bugs. Cosmetic emoji-encoding issue noted under action_items: 🆘 codepoint U+1F198 (4 bytes UTF-8 F0 9F 86 98) becomes URL-encoded %EF%BF%BD in the WhatsApp share link, while the em-dash U+2014 (3 bytes) survives correctly. Likely a 4-byte surrogate handling problem in a downstream serializer or a non-UTF-8 source read step — investigate FastAPI response.encoding / file BOM / any string.encode('latin-1', 'replace') in the share-message path.
